title: Zero-section divisor class, its etale realization, and compact source
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ and uniformizer $\varpi_F$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $\pi:E\to B$ a vector bundle of rank one with zero section $z:B\to E$ [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Use the prescribed pro-etale twist $A_T(1)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Then $\pi$ is separated of finite type and smooth of relative dimension one, and $D=z(B)$ is an effective Cartier divisor, smooth over $B$ of relative codimension one, which remains Cartier after every base change $B'\to B$ of the bundle and its zero section.

Let $c^{p}_{D,A}:z_*A_B\to A_E(1)[2]$ be the supported Cartier Kummer morphism of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]. Under the supported-class realization of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], the relative Kummer class $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ of [lem-pur-divisor-class] is exactly $c^{p}_{D,A}$. Its local supported class in a bundle coordinate $t$ is $-\partial\kappa(t)$, with $\kappa$ and the support boundary in the conventions of [def-pur-frame-class] and [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary].

Put $N=\ell^n$, which kills $A$, and $L_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, where $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}$ is the sheaf of $N$th roots of unity. Let $c^e_{D,A}:z_*A_B\to L_E[2]$ be the ordinary etale supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. With $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], the projection-induced twist comparison $\nu_T^*L_T\cong A_T(1)$ carries $\nu_E^*c^e_{D,A}$ to $c^p_{D,A}$.

Under the canonical identity-normalized composition identification $R\pi_!z_*A_B\cong A_B$, the map $\tau_E=R\pi_!c^p_{D,A}$ is the realization of $R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}c^e_{D,A}$, with source $A_B$ and target $R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_E[2]$, through the comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. In particular the map itself, with these specified source and target identifications, has a bounded-below etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. No invertibility of $\tau_E$ is asserted.

proof.text: Write the bundle as the relative spectrum of the symmetric algebra using [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. The locally free rank-one module admits a Zariski affine trivializing cover; [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] identifies the projection and zero section on each member $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and the quotient $R[t]\to R$, $t\mapsto0$. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-amb-vector-projective-completion] to this rank-one locally free module, transporting its construction through the chosen total-space isomorphism: it gives a projective completion of $E$, and asserts that $\pi$ is separated and finite type and $E$ Noetherian. These are the compactification and finiteness hypotheses needed below. To check the absolute hypotheses, choose a finite affine trivializing cover of $B$ with coordinate rings finitely generated over $k$. Then $E$ has the corresponding finite affine cover with rings $R[t]$, also finitely generated over $k$, so it is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its absolute diagonal factors through $E\times_BE$: the first arrow is the closed relative diagonal of $\pi$, and the second is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $B/k$. On affine charts these are quotients of rings; tensoring a surjection and composing surjections preserve surjectivity. Thus $E/k$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Step 1: global Cartier zero divisor and global morphism

proof.text: On the charts in step 1, [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] with rank one proves smoothness of relative dimension one. Smoothness and that fibre dimension are affine-local in the equivalent affine-local definition of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so this proves the assertion for $\pi$. Since $\pi z=1$, $D\to B$ is the identity and is smooth of relative dimension zero. Its ideal on a chart is $(t)$; if $tg=0$ in $R[t]$, comparison of coefficients gives $g=0$. Thus it is an effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. At a point of $D$, $t$ stays a nonzerodivisor in the Noetherian local ring of $E$, and quotient by $t$ is the local ring of $D$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to obtain pure codimension one. For every $B'\to B$, restrict to affine charts over the cover just used: the pullback equation is again $t$ in $R'[t]$, with quotient $R'$. The same coefficient argument proves the Cartier property without flatness or Noetherianity of $B'$. This is base change of the bundle over $B$, not arbitrary pullback into $E$.

source.place: Step 1: global Cartier zero divisor and global morphism

proof.text: Put $N=\ell^n$. Since $\ell\in(\varpi_F)$, $\ell^n\in(\varpi_F^n)$ and $NA=0$; $N$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme under consideration. Apply [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] first with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z/N$ to see that $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}$ is flat over $(\mathbf Z/N)_T$. Hence its derived tensor with $A_T$ is the ordinary tensor in degree zero, so the $L_T$ in the statement is a bounded-below ordinary etale complex, also when $A$ is not flat over $\mathbf Z/N$. Apply [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] with annihilating exponent $n$ to obtain the projection-induced isomorphism $\theta_T:\nu_T^*L_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T(1)$. The projection convention is precisely the one specified in [def-pur-frame-class]; this keeps the prescribed pro-etale twist rather than redefining it.

source.place: Step 1: global Cartier zero divisor and global morphism

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] to $D\hookrightarrow E$, $N$, and $A$; all its hypotheses were checked in steps 1--3. It gives $c^e_{D,A}:z_*A_B\to L_E[2]$ by the relative line bundle $\mathcal O_E(D)$ with its canonical section off $D$, followed by derived scalar extension. Apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] to the same divisor and coefficient ring. Its stated etale witness uses the same roots-of-unity sheaf and the same supported morphism; its definition is etale Kummer followed by comparison pullback and the projection-induced twist identification. Consequently, under its canonical supported-constant source comparison, $c^p_{D,A}=\theta_E[2]\circ\nu_E^*c^e_{D,A}$. This equality compares the actual supported relative construction, not just its image after forgetting support.

source.place: Step 1: global Cartier zero divisor and global morphism

proof.text: By [lem-pur-divisor-class], whose hypotheses hold by steps 1--2 ($E\to B$ smooth of relative dimension one, $D$ smooth over $B$ of pure codimension one, $E$ separated of finite type over $k$), the class $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ is the relative Kummer boundary of $\mathcal O_E(D)$ with its canonical trivialization off $D$, in the Yoneda convention of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. Apply [lem-pur-cartier-class-agreement] to the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T=E$ and the effective Cartier divisor $D$ of step 2: under the natural supported-Hom isomorphism $H^2_D(E,A(1))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(z_*A_B,A_E(1)[2])$ of [lem-pur-supported-hom] (at $F=A_E(1)$, in degree zero by step 3, and degree two), $\operatorname{cl}(D)$ is the morphism $c^p_{D,A}$ of [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], with the relative-torsor normalization through derived scalar extension and the roots projection of [def-pur-frame-class] that step 4 uses. For smooth $D$ the general Cartier construction of [lem-pur-divisor-class] used there is the same relative construction as its first paragraph. The local equation on a bundle chart is $t$; the displayed local formula of [lem-pur-divisor-class] gives $-\partial\kappa(t)$. The Kummer class here is the prescribed one of [def-pur-frame-class]. In particular the sign is inherited from the already corrected divisor-class statement, not from the older blueprint's positive frame-class formula.

source.place: Step 1: global Cartier zero divisor and global morphism

proof.text: For the closed immersion $z$, use the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_B,z)$. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). The ordinary etale identification $Rz_!\cong z_*$ is provided by [lem-pur-closed-finite-adjoint-counit-transport]. On the pro-etale site [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] gives $Rz_*=z_*$; its quasi-compact-complement hypothesis holds since $E$ is Noetherian. Thus the same identity/proper compactification gives $Rz_!=z_*$. Apply the composition isomorphisms [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and [thm-sf-comp-composition] to $B\xrightarrow z E\xrightarrow\pi B$. Since $\pi z=\mathrm{id}_B$, they identify $R\pi_!z_*A_B$ with $R(\pi z)_!A_B=A_B$ in the two topologies, using the canonical identity normalization. The ordinary etale supported source $z_*A_B$ is in degree zero, so these uses lie in $D^+$.

proof.text:
Let $ eta_M:
u_B^*R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_!
u_E^*M$ denote the inverse-direction form of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison], for the projective completion of step 1. Both $M=z_*A_B$ and $M=L_E[2]$ are bounded below. Its naturality applied to $c^e=c^e_{D,A}$ gives
$$ eta_{L_E[2]}\circ
u_B^*(R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}c^e)=R\pi_!(
u_E^*c^e)\circ eta_{z_*A_B}.$$
By [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence], the source component of this equation respects the composition for $\pi z$ and the identity, so step 6 identifies it with the canonical constant-sheaf comparison $
u_B^*A_B\cong A_B$. Substitute the equality of step 4 and then the target comparison $R\pi_!	heta_E[2]$. The right side is exactly $	au_E=R\pi_!c^p_{D,A}$, with the prescribed source $A_B$. The left side exhibits its etale representative $R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}c^e:A_B	o R\pi_!^{\mathrm{et}}L_E[2]$. The target is bounded below by the compact-support comparison's $D^+$ assertion. Retaining that representative and these two comparison isomorphisms is the witness of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] for the actual map. Nothing in this argument asserts that $	au_E$ is invertible.
